explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/673: with G(n) = Σ_{i<τ(n)} d_i/d_{i+1}, is G(n) → ∞ for almost all n? Yes; Tao's bounds make it trivial, and Erdős recalled this in [Er82e]. G is defined via Nat.nth (· ∣ n), which lists divisors from d_1 = 1 for n > 0. The statement asserts that {n : C < G n} has density 1 for every C, the standard 'almost all' reading. Faithful.
